new.title: See the 1472 astronomical clock in the Marienkirche
new.desc: The Marienkirche is Rostock's main parish church, a huge brick Gothic basilica from the 13th to 15th century. Behind the high altar stands the astronomical clock of 1472, which still shows hours, weekdays, zodiac signs and moon phases with its original medieval works.
new.tip: Open daily for visitors, with a small admission fee for the clock area; the clock's apostle procession runs at noon. Combine with a walk across the Neuer Markt.

new.title: Walk through the Kröpeliner Tor and its fortification museum
new.desc: The six-storey Kröpeliner Tor, built around 1270, is the tallest gate of Rostock's medieval city wall at about 54 metres, with four stepped gables. An exhibition inside covers the history of the city fortifications.
new.tip: It closes the pedestrian Kröpeliner Straße at its western end. Check the exhibition opening hours as they vary by season.

new.title: Visit the Kulturhistorisches Museum in the Heiligen Kreuz monastery
new.desc: The Kloster zum Heiligen Kreuz is the only fully preserved monastery complex in Rostock, founded in 1270 according to tradition by Queen Margaret of Denmark. Today it houses the Kulturhistorisches Museum, with the history of the Hanseatic city, medieval art and a large coin collection.
new.tip: Closed on Mondays in most seasons, so check before going. Allow about 90 minutes.

new.title: Climb the Petrikirche tower for a view over Rostock
new.desc: St. Petri is a brick Gothic church whose 117-metre tower was a sea mark for sailors. An observation platform at 45 metres, reached by lift or about 196 steps, gives a full all-round view over the old town, harbour and the coast.
new.tip: Best on a clear day; the lift saves the stairs. Check opening hours as the church closes in winter.

new.title: Admire the Rathaus and its seven towers on the Neuer Markt
new.desc: Rostock's town hall is a Gothic brick building from the 13th century, to which a Baroque front was added in 1727. Only seven slender towers of the original facade remain visible above it. It stands on the Neuer Markt beside gabled merchant houses.
new.tip: Free to view from the square. Pair with the nearby Marienkirche.

new.title: Find the Steintor, the old southern gate
new.desc: The Steintor is a Gothic gate on Steinstraße that once served as the southern main gate of Rostock. Its Renaissance gable was added later and it is one of four surviving gates of the city wall.
new.tip: Free and a short walk from the Rathaus; look for the sections of wall nearby.

new.title: Meet at the Brunnen der Lebensfreude on the Universitätsplatz
new.desc: The University of Rostock was founded in 1419 and is the third-oldest in Germany; its main building dates from 1867 to 1870. In front stands the Brunnen der Lebensfreude by Jo Jastram, one of the city's favourite meeting points.
new.tip: Free and central, right off Kröpeliner Straße. Lively with students on sunny days.

new.title: Step inside the Nikolaikirche, the oldest church in the old town
new.desc: St. Nikolai is a typical example of North German brick Gothic, founded in the 13th century as the church of the merchants. It has been used for concerts and events in recent years.
new.tip: Opening times vary, so check at the site. Free to enter when open.

new.title: Climb the Warnemünde lighthouse
new.desc: The Warnemünde lighthouse dates from 1898 and stands 37 metres tall on the seafront, beside the Teepott. The gallery looks over the harbour entrance, the Alter Strom and the beach, and the tower is run by a volunteer association.
new.tip: Open for visitors from about Easter to early October; a small admission fee applies. The nearby Teepott makes a good coffee stop.

new.title: See the Teepott shell roof by Ulrich Müther
new.desc: The Teepott is a concrete shell building from 1968, designed by Ulrich Müther, with a striking curved hyperbolic-paraboloid roof. It houses restaurants and cafés beside the lighthouse and looks over the sea.
new.tip: Free to look at; step inside for a drink with a sea view.

new.title: Stroll the Alter Strom in Warnemünde
new.desc: The Alter Strom is the old harbour channel of Warnemünde, lined with fishermen's cottages, fish cutters and restaurants. It is the postcard heart of the seaside resort and is described by guides as the classic Warnemünde walk.
new.tip: Come early for fewer crowds; the fish stalls here are good for lunch.

new.title: See contemporary art at the Kunsthalle Rostock
new.desc: The Kunsthalle Rostock is a purpose-built GDR gallery from 1969 on the Schwanenteich park, with a modern-art programme. It has been run as a non-profit company since 2024.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 11 to 18, per current listings; check for current exhibitions.

new.title: Board the MS Dresden at the Schifffahrtsmuseum
new.desc: The Schiffbau- und Schifffahrtsmuseum is housed on the former GDR cargo ship Dresden in the IGA Park. It documents shipbuilding and seafaring history with exhibits on the ship.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 10 to 16 from November to March and 10 to 18 from April to October.

new.title: Walk the IGA Park on the Warnow
new.desc: The IGA Park was created for the International Horticultural Exhibition of 2003 and lies on the western bank of the Warnow. It combines gardens, a lake and the museum ship Dresden.
new.tip: Open 8 to 17 from November to March and 8 to 22 from April to October.

new.title: Eat fish at Zur Kogge, a red-gabled harbour tavern
new.desc: Zur Kogge is a red-gabled house near the Stadthafen on Wokrenterstraße, listed in guides as one of Rostock's oldest taverns. It serves hearty fish and Mecklenburg dishes at fair prices.
new.tip: Order the fish of the day; reserve in the evening. Verify current hours before going.

new.title: Dine on fish at Otto's Restaurantschiff in the Stadthafen
new.desc: Otto's is a converted ship moored at the Stadthafen with panoramic views over the harbour. The menu runs from zander and salmon to vegan bowls.
new.tip: Take a table on deck in summer; try the zander.
new.q: Otto's Restaurant und Hafenbar, Stadthafen 70, Rostock

new.title: Order the Dreierlei Fischfilet at the Borwin Hafenrestaurant
new.desc: The Borwin Hafenrestaurant sits on Am Strande beside the Stadthafen. The house recommendations include a trio of fish fillets with asparagus.
new.tip: Ask for a harbour-view table.

new.title: Drink house-brewed beer at Brauhaus Trotzenburg
new.desc: The Forsthausbrauerei Trotzenburg is a brewpub in a historic forester's lodge on Tiergartenallee, converted to brew its own beer in 2001, with a beer garden. It brews Rostock beer on site.
new.tip: Try the house-brewed beer in the beer garden. Hours reported as 11 to 23; call 0381 203600 to confirm.

new.title: Eat a Bismarck or Backfisch roll at Backfisch Udo
new.desc: Backfisch Udo is a fish stall on the Alter Strom in Warnemünde serving Fischbrötchen. A Bismarck herring roll costs about 4.50 euro in reviews.
new.tip: Prices rise in season; the Bismarck roll is the classic order.

new.title: Eat smoked fish at Fischhus min Herzing near the beach
new.desc: Fischhus min Herzing is a fish snack spot near the Warnemünde beach, serving rolls and fish dishes.
new.tip: Handy after the beach; check opening hours as they follow the season.

new.title: Get a scoop at the Eiswerkstatt on Kröpeliner Straße
new.desc: The Eiswerkstatt is an ice-cream shop at Kröpeliner Straße 18 in the pedestrian zone of the old town.
new.tip: A good stop on the walk between Neuer Markt and Kröpeliner Tor.

new.title: Have coffee at Café Central in the KTV
new.desc: Café Central is a neighbourhood café on Leonhardstraße in the Kröpeliner-Tor-Vorstadt, the student quarter.
new.tip: A relaxed place for breakfast or coffee in the KTV.

new.title: Have a cocktail at the Stadtkind bar
new.desc: Stadtkind is a cosy, warmly designed bar on Leonhardstraße in the KTV, described as feeling like a comfortable living room.
new.tip: Evening drinks; busy at weekends.

new.title: Sip cocktails at the Craftbar on Margaretenstraße
new.desc: The Craftbar Rostock is a cocktail bar on Margaretenstraße in the KTV, praised for drink quality.
new.tip: Ask for the bartender's pick.

new.title: Spend a day on the Warnemünde beach
new.desc: The Warnemünde beach is a wide, fine-sand Baltic beach several kilometres long, running from the Alter Strom to the west, with beach baskets and a seafront promenade.
new.tip: Swimming season is summer; walk the promenade to the lighthouse.

new.title: Swim at the quieter Markgrafenheide beach
new.desc: Markgrafenheide lies on the eastern side of the Warnow mouth at the edge of the Rostocker Heide, with dunes and a sandy Baltic beach, calmer than Warnemünde.
new.tip: Reach it by the Warnemünde ferry then by bus or bike.

new.title: Hike the Hütelmoor and dunes loop from Markgrafenheide
new.desc: A loop of about 11 km runs from Markgrafenheide between the dunes and the Heiligensee and Hütelmoor nature reserve, with viewpoints and beach access points along the coast.
new.tip: Rated easy; wear sturdy shoes and follow the dog rules in the reserve.

new.title: Cycle through the Rostocker Heide
new.desc: The Rostocker Heide covers about 6,000 hectares of forest between Markgrafenheide and Graal-Müritz. The Baltic coast cycle path leads across it, partly paved and partly sandy.
new.tip: Take the ferry from Warnemünde and ride east along the coast.

new.title: Browse the Rostocker Weihnachtsmarkt
new.desc: The Rostock Christmas market fills the old town between the Neuer Markt and the Kröpeliner Straße, with a Ferris wheel of about 34 metres. Entry is free.
new.tip: Listed for late November to 22 December 2026; check official dates.

new.title: Cross the Warnow on the Warnemünde ferry to Hohe Düne
new.desc: A passenger ferry links Warnemünde with Hohe Düne and Markgrafenheide across the Warnow mouth, with a view of the ships entering the port.
new.tip: Check the operator's timetable before relying on it.

new.title: Take a harbour cruise from Warnemünde
new.desc: Harbour cruises of around 100 minutes run along the Alter Strom and through the Rostock overseas harbour, passing cruise ships and ferries.
new.tip: Price reported around 20 euro; confirm with the operator.

new.title: Visit the Darwineum at Zoo Rostock
new.desc: Zoo Rostock is home to the Darwineum, a combined exhibit on evolution with apes, penguins and a tropical hall.
new.tip: Check the current hours on the zoo website.

new.title: Walk the Stadthafen promenade
new.desc: The Stadthafen runs along the Warnow, with museum and sail ships, restaurants and the old town behind.
new.tip: A nice evening walk; a ferry loop is possible.

new.title: Walk the West Mole at the Warnemünde harbour entrance
new.desc: The long breakwater mole at the mouth of the Alter Strom lets you walk out between the sea and the harbour channel, with ships passing close.
new.tip: Bring a windbreaker; free.
